valid_owner_signature_exists.meaning: a valid on-chain ECDSA signature from the AtomWallet owner exists and is observable

high_s_signature_derivable.meaning: an observer can derive a high-s counterpart (s' = curve_order - s, v' = v XOR 1) recovering the identical signer address

high_s_triggers_invalid_s_branch.meaning: a high-s signature causes OpenZeppelin ECDSA tryRecover to return RecoverError.InvalidSignatureS

bundler_disruption_occurs.meaning: bundler simulation failures waste compute and may cause retries or blacklisting of the targeted wallet

assumptions: The high-s signature is a 65-byte signature in scope (README known issue covers only signature length, not s-value canonicity).
EntryPoint calls validateUserOp without try/catch during handleOps.
The adversary is an observer of the public on-chain signature and submits griefing UserOps.

unresolved.description: Report describes bundler disruption impacts as potential; no observed griefing transaction or concrete retry/blacklisting outcome is stated, so the disruption observable is a qualitative Boolean.
Whether the validation revert propagates to handleOps and causes bundler simulation failure depends on EntryPoint version and bundler implementation, which the report does not fix.

limitations: The bundler disruption impact is formalized as a qualitative Boolean because the report gives no numeric definition of compute waste, retries, or blacklisting.
Only the i_bundler_disruption impact is formalized; bundle revert and wallet degradation impacts are handled in separate passes.
The condition encodes the concrete high-s scenario; the intent's general 'signature mismatch' scope is represented only through this subcase.
